tagline: From the Hallyeo waterway to Jeju — a peninsula that already lives on its super-app.
summary: Korea pairs a dense, mobile-first population with a coastline built for marine mobility: the scenic Hallyeo maritime corridor linking Busan, Geoje, Tongyeong and Yeosu, and Jeju — the country's signature island, reached today by the world's busiest air shuttle and by conventional ferries. With a super-app like Kakao Mobility already orchestrating how Koreans move, a clean foiling water tier is the natural next layer, not a new habit to teach.
why_marine_mobility: Korea's coastal story is two corridors. The first is the Hallyeo waterway — a sheltered, island-studded national-park sea between Busan/Geoje and Yeosu/Tongyeong that draws heavy domestic tourism and runs on slow local ferries. The second is Jeju: the busiest leisure destination in the country, served by a saturated Gimpo–Jeju air corridor and long mainland ferries. Navier's Pioneer II turns the Hallyeo hops into smooth, dry, on-demand crossings, while the Quanta-LR's range opens the Busan–Jeju sea trunk that no battery day-boat can serve — both surfaced through a mobility platform Koreans already open every day.

demand_signals.label: Super-app distribution
demand_signals.note: Korea's mobility demand is already aggregated inside dominant super-apps such as Kakao Mobility — a ready demand-and-booking layer for an on-demand water tier rather than a cold-start market.

demand_signals.label: Hallyeo maritime-park volume
demand_signals.note: The Hallyeo-Haesang corridor between Busan, Geoje, Tongyeong and Yeosu is a heavily visited coastal national park whose island hops run entirely on conventional ferries.

demand_signals.label: Jeju connectivity pressure
demand_signals.note: Jeju is reached by one of the world's most congested air shuttles and by slow mainland ferries; a fast clean sea link is a genuine relief valve for an over-served corridor.

use_cases.body: Busan/Geoje to Yeosu/Tongyeong: a Hallyeo-corridor hop bookable in-app on Pioneer II, replacing a slow local ferry with a smooth, dry, on-demand crossing surfaced through the super-app Koreans already use.
Busan/Geoje to Jeju: a long-range Quanta-LR sea trunk linking the mainland to the country's flagship island — a clean alternative to the saturated air shuttle that no day-boat can run.
Jeju resort-coast hops around Seogwipo and Jungmun: short, scenic foiling legs along the island's premium hotel coast, flown quiet and emission-free for a high-end leisure audience.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Hallyeo-corridor legs between Busan/Geoje and Yeosu/Tongyeong (~3–11 nm) and the Jeju resort-coast hops sit well inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots — commercial-ready today and a direct upgrade on local ferries.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Busan/Geoje–Jeju sea trunk (~157 nm) is Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening a mainland-to-island corridor no all-electric day-boat can reach.

signature_routes.label: Busan/Geoje ↔ Jeju — the long-range island sea trunk
Busan/Geoje ↔ Yeosu/Tongyeong — the Hallyeo maritime corridor

transit_planning: For a mobility platform or a regional authority: a clean, on-demand water tier that plugs into an existing super-app booking layer rather than building demand from scratch. Start with the Hallyeo-corridor and Jeju coastal hops on Pioneer II — commercial today — then add the Busan–Jeju sea trunk on Quanta-LR as hybrid range comes online, relieving an air corridor already at its limits.
competitive_landscape: Coastal and island travel today runs on conventional local ferries (reliable, affordable, but slow, fixed-schedule and diesel) and, for Jeju, on a saturated air shuttle. There is no on-demand premium water tier. Navier's foiling craft is the missing premium-but-practical layer — faster and smoother than a ferry, cleaner than diesel craft, and distributable through a mobility platform that already owns the Korean rider relationship.
regulatory_note: Domestic maritime passenger transport is regulated by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) and the Korea Coast Guard, with vessel certification and coastal-route licensing required. Jeju Special Self-Governing Province has its own provincial authority and is a natural first touchpoint for the island corridor.
seasonality: The Hallyeo waterway is sheltered and navigable most of the year, with peak demand in spring and autumn; the main weather risk is the summer typhoon window (peak Jul–Sep). Jeju demand peaks in summer and over holiday periods. A stabilised foiling craft holds comfort and schedule across choppy shoulder-season conditions when conventional ferries are most disrupted.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium, low-emission water-shuttle model Navier brings to Korea's coastal and island corridors.

sources.label: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), Republic of Korea
